You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 640d7efe4c08f06c4ae5d31b79bd8740e7f6790a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ben Hutchings <ben@decadent.org.uk>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2014 00:06:48 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] dns_resolver: Null-terminate the right string

*_result[len] is parsed as *(_result[len]) which is not at all what we
want to touch here.

Signed-off-by: Ben Hutchings <ben@decadent.org.uk>
Fixes: 84a7c0b1db1c ("dns_resolver: assure that dns_query() result is null-terminated")
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
---
 net/dns_resolver/dns_query.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/net/dns_resolver/dns_query.c b/net/dns_resolver/dns_query.c
index 9acec61f5433..dd8696a3dbec 100644
--- a/net/dns_resolver/dns_query.c
+++ b/net/dns_resolver/dns_query.c
@@ -150,7 +150,7 @@ int dns_query(const char *type, const char *name, size_t namelen,
 		goto put;
 
 	memcpy(*_result, upayload->data, len);
-	*_result[len] = '\0';
+	(*_result)[len] = '\0';
 
 	if (_expiry)
 		*_expiry = rkey->expiry;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The original code incorrectly attempted to null-terminate the result string by accessing it as *_result[len], which evaluated the value at the memory location rather than correctly accessing the string's character array. This caused undefined behavior because it mistakenly interpreted it as an indexed value. The fix was to correctly dereference the pointer and access it with (*_result)[len], ensuring that the null termination is applied to the right location in the string.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The original code incorrectly attempted to null-terminate the result string by accessing it as *_result[len], which evaluated the value at the memory location rather than correctly accessing the string's character array. This caused undefined behavior because it mistakenly interpreted it as an indexed value. The fix was to correctly dereference the pointer and access it with (*_result)[len], ensuring that the null termination is applied to the right location in the string.
